title: Stateless Protocol
body:
Request + Response is self contained. It is unconnected to previous requests.

[[HTTP]] is stateless: the server does not remember that the request it handled a second ago came from the same person. Every request must carry everything needed to serve it — which credentials, which resource, which page of results. Two consecutive requests from the same browser look, to the server, like two unrelated strangers.

This is a deliberate design choice, not an oversight. It's what lets any of a hundred machines behind a [[Load Balancer]] handle your next request without needing to share conversational memory, and it's a large part of why the web scales.

The cost is that anything resembling a session has to be reconstructed on every request, from something the client sends along: a cookie, a token, an API key. That's exactly the problem [[Cookies]] were invented to solve.
